# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 44 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 44 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_044_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 1 — Resist Evil Desire

**44:1** He said to me: "Remove from yourself every evil desire and clothe yourself with the desire that is good and holy. For if you clothe yourself with this good desire, you will hate the evil desire and will bridle it as you choose. For the evil desire is savage and is subdued with great difficulty. It is terrible and consumes men greatly by its savagery. And a servant of God is consumed by it above all, if he does not know how to employ it rightly."

**44:2** "What then are the works of the evil desire that overthrow the servants of God?" I asked. "Tell me, that I may keep away from them." "Listen," he said, "to the works by which the evil desire puts to death those who serve God."

**44:3** "Foremost is the desire for another man's wife or another woman's husband; then extravagance in wealth, and the craving for many unnecessary foods and drinks, and for many other foolish luxuries. For every luxury is foolish and empty for the servants of God. These desires, therefore, are evil and produce death for the servants of God. For this evil desire is a daughter of the devil. You must therefore keep away from evil desires, so that by keeping away from them you may live to God."

**44:4** "But those who are dominated by these desires and do not resist them shall perish utterly, for these desires lead to death. But you who follow righteousness and virtue — clothe yourself with desire for these things, and renouncing every evil desire, put on the desire that is good and honorable and acceptable before God, and you shall live to God, every one of you who lives in this way."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and ethical precision.*
